premises.text: Doctors make bad decisions because they lack a way to share their experience.
premises.evidence_span: Good doctors like me and Mark wind up making bad decisions because we have no way to share our experience.

premises.text: Existing reference tools do not provide sufficient information for doctors.
premises.evidence_span: Doctors don't have time to read every single journal article. It's an antiquated model, so we rely on reference tools to synthesize information for us.

premises.text: SharePractice allows doctors to rank treatments based on their experiences.
premises.evidence_span: these treatments are actually ranked by doctors upvoting and downvoting these treatments.

premises.text: SharePractice provides clinically relevant information needed for prescriptions.
premises.evidence_span: you have comments from other doctors telling you why this is the best choice.

premises.text: SharePractice captures unique data on treatment choices that is not available elsewhere.
A proprietary medical ontology allows SharePractice to make sense of medical terminology.
premises.evidence_span: share practice built a proprietary medical ontology that took multiple databases.

value.text: Patients receive better treatment through shared doctor experiences.
value.evidence_span: you can be confident that you're going to get the best treatment because effectively, share practice puts a million doctors in every doctor's pocket.

notes: No separate premises for the viral model as it is part of the user engagement strategy.
